title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, claiming your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information. They may sound urgent or threatening to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare calling. There is a problem with your account and your benefits will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security or Medicare number
Pressures you to act right away
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you are concerned.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text message saying there is a problem with a package delivery and you need to click a link. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information or installs malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your address by clicking here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to a website you don't recognize
Requests for personal or payment information
what_to_do: Do not click any links; delete the message.

title: Facebook Friend Impersonation Scam
how_it_works: Scammers create fake Facebook profiles using your friends' names and photos. They send you messages asking for money or personal information, pretending to be your friend in need.
example_message: "Hi, it's me! I need your help. Can you send me $200 right away? I'll pay you back soon."
red_flags: Friend's profile looks new or has few posts
what_to_do: Contact your friend directly by phone to check if the request is real.

title: Romance Scam on Dating Sites
how_it_works: A scammer pretends to be interested in a romantic relationship online. After gaining your trust, they ask for money, often claiming an emergency or travel problem.
example_message: "I really care about you, but I need help paying for a plane ticket to come see you. Can you send me some money?"
red_flags: Claims to be overseas or unable to meet in person
Makes excuses for not video chatting
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven't met in person.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and need to call a number for help. The scammer on the phone asks for remote access or payment to 'fix' your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Asks to control your computer remotely
Requests payment in gift cards or wire transfer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; use your own trusted tech support if you need help.
